subject.title: Feature: Subscribe to WhatsApp call events (Baileys)

question: Should the first inbound WhatsApp call implementation expose transient sanitized events only, or also persist per-contact call history?
rationale: Persistence changes privacy, retention, storage, identity, deduplication, migration, configuration, and agent API contracts, and current OpenClaw has no canonical model for that data.

options.title: Transient events first
options.body: Add the exact Baileys listener, normalization, access controls, cleanup, opt-in exposure, and tests without retaining call history.

options.title: Design durable history
options.body: Approve a canonical contact-activity store and query API before implementing persistence.

options.title: Do not ingest calls
options.body: Leave call events unsupported if this sensitive activity metadata is outside product scope.

recommendation.title: Transient events first
recommendation.body: Add the exact Baileys listener, normalization, access controls, cleanup, opt-in exposure, and tests without retaining call history.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-specific history combines the monitor refactor, recent call implementation, and direct issue scoping.
